name: MS-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+18 district lean in deep-red northeast Mississippi
Incumbent Trent Kelly running for reelection with a large cash advantage
No polls or expert ratings; markets price Kelly at ~96%
Challenger Cliff Johnson outraised roughly two-to-one but trails badly in cash
model.rationale: Kelly holds a seat that leans Republican by about 18 points, has won comfortably in prior cycles, and carries a strong fundraising edge over Johnson. With no polling, no expert ratings, and markets pricing his win near 96%, there is no evidence to move the race off its fundamentals.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing Johnson within single digits, or a surge of outside spending against Kelly, would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Trent Kelly seeks another term in a northeast Mississippi district that has voted Republican by wide margins for years. He enters the general election as a well-funded incumbent, with more than $860,000 on hand after raising over $1 million. Democrat Cliff Johnson has run a credible campaign for a challenger in this territory, raising about $550,000, but he trails in cash and faces a steep partisan landscape.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Kelly roughly a 96% chance of winning. Absent unexpected developments, the seat is expected to remain in Republican hands by a margin in the high teens.
